notes: Confirms title. 3 sheets, 5 word problems per sheet with clip-art.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 24 Multi-digit Addition Word Problems Adding Large Numbers
does: 5 word problems per sheet ('Large Numbers Addition') adding two multi-digit numbers well beyond 3 digits, including dollar amounts in the tens of millions (e.g. $30,700,565 + $45,565,700), 5-digit marathon participant counts (20,144+17,038), and 4-digit package/restaurant counts; students write the answer on a blank line.
notes: Numbers (tens of millions) are far beyond typical Grade 2 standard scope (2.NBT.B.7 covers up to 1000); this sheet is likely a stretch/enrichment worksheet mislabeled by grade, or is meant only for place-value/addition procedure practice, not standard mastery. Uses US dollar amounts and a named US event (Chicago Marathon).

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 25 3-digit and 2-digit Addition with Word Problems No Regrouping
does: Five sheets (S1-S5), each with 12 vertical 3-digit-plus-2-digit column addition problems with no regrouping, plus 2 short word problems involving money ($) or real-life counts at the end of each sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 26 Solving 3-Digit and 2-Digit Addition Word Problems
does: Three sheets, each with 5 short word problems requiring addition of a 3-digit and a 2-digit number (e.g. miles traveled, books lent, dollars spent); some involve an extra 'more than' comparison step.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 27 Finding the Sum of 3-Digit Numbers with Word Problems
does: Five sheets (S1-S5), each with 12 vertical 3-digit addition column problems (no regrouping) plus 2 short word problems finding the sum of two 3-digit quantities.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 28 3-Digit Addition Word Problems
does: Three sheets, each with 5 word problems requiring addition of two 3-digit numbers (no computation grid, word-problems only), themed around collections, purchases, and counts.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 29 Completing Addition Sentences Treasure Box
does: Three sheets (Easy S1-S3), each with 8 addition number sentences with a missing addend or sum to complete (3-digit + 3-digit = sum format), 'Treasure Box' themed.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 30 2-Digit Addition Word Problems No Regrouping
does: Three sheets, each with 5 word problems requiring 2-digit plus 2-digit addition with no regrouping, in real-life scenarios (baking, shopping, animals).

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 31 2-Digit Addition Word Problems Regrouping
does: Three sheets, each with 5 word problems requiring 2-digit plus 2-digit addition with regrouping, in real-life scenarios (sports, music, shopping, costumes).
notes: Sheet titles inconsistently say 'No Regrouping' vs 'Regrouping' across sheets, but folder title and most problems indicate regrouping is required; a teacher should preview problems that need carrying.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 32 Addition Properties Revision Sums within 20
does: 8 problem-pairs per sheet, each showing two equivalent addition expressions (e.g. 2+1 and 1+2; (9+3)+6 and 9+(3+6)); students find each sum and name the property demonstrated (commutative or associative), sums within 20.
notes: Corrects original guess of 'fact families': content is explicitly commutative AND associative property pairs, not fact families. 3 sheets, 8 pairs per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 33 Logic Addition Puzzles
does: Nine 2x2 blank grids per sheet, each labeled with a row-sum to the right of each row and a column-sum below each column (no interior values given); students figure out four single-digit numbers to fill the grid that satisfy both the row and column sums.
notes: Confirms puzzle format; unlike the 'Addition Squares' series, no headers/interior values are given at all, only the row/column totals, so students must reason out a consistent set of 4 numbers. 5 sheets, 9 puzzles per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 34 Adding with Base Ten Blocks
does: 8 problems per sheet, each showing two groups of base-ten block pictures (tens rods and ones cubes, in two colors); students write each group's value in a blank box, then write the sum in a third blank box (box + box = box format).
notes: Confirms title and format. 3 sheets, 8 problems per sheet, no visible text instructions beyond the title and blank boxes.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 35 Two-Digit Addition - No Regrouping
does: 12 vertical (stacked) two-digit plus two-digit addition problems with no regrouping needed, plus 2 word problems at the bottom of each sheet.
notes: No themed/pictorial layout as previously guessed - it is a plain numeric column-addition drill with 2 word problems appended. 5 sheets, 12 problems + 2 word problems per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Addition - 36 Two-Digit Addition With Regrouping - Standard
does: 12 vertical (stacked) two-digit plus two-digit addition problems requiring regrouping, plus 2 word problems at the bottom of each sheet, same layout as sheet 35.
notes: Confirms title. 5 sheets, 12 problems + 2 word problems per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 01 Area of Rectilinear Figures Set
does: Five sheets (L1S1-L1S5), each with 15 rectilinear (composite/L-shaped) figures drawn on unit-square grids; students find area by counting whole unit squares. Units alternate ft², in², yd² by sheet.
notes: Grade-2-appropriate readiness activity for area concepts (formal area standards begin in Grade 3).

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 02 Area of Shapes by Counting Unit Squares Set
does: 'Counting Squares' worksheet: 9 irregular polyomino shapes drawn on a grid per sheet (each square = 1 square unit, no specific unit of measure given); students count the shaded squares and write the area in the blank.
notes: No 'ft²' or other specific unit is shown on this sheet - the legend just says '1 square unit' (generic, unitless). 5 sheets, 9 shapes per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 03 Area of Shapes by Counting Unit Squares Set
does: Same 'Counting Squares' format as sheet 02, but with 9 solid-colored polygon/silhouette shapes per sheet (e.g. boat, star, house, car, octagon) drawn on a grid; students count squares to find the area.
notes: 5 sheets, 9 shapes per sheet, generic unitless squares.

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 04 Area of Shapes by Counting Unit Squares Set
does: 'Counting Squares' worksheet with 12 plain rectangles per sheet, each divided into a labeled grid (1 in² per square); students count the squares to find each rectangle's area.
notes: Unlike sheets 02/03 (irregular shapes, unitless), this sheet uses plain rectangles with an explicit 'in²' unit. 5 sheets, 12 rectangles per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 05 Perimeter of a Rectangle Set
does: Five sheets (T1L1S1-S5), each with 9 rectangles labeled with two side lengths; students calculate the perimeter of each rectangle by adding all four sides.
notes: Perimeter is formally a Grade-3 CCSS standard; likely used here as an early-exposure/enrichment topic in this Grade-2 folder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Area & Perimeter - 06 Perimeter of a Square Set
does: Five sheets (T1L1S1-S5), each with 9 squares labeled with one side length; students calculate the perimeter of each square by multiplying/adding the side length by 4.
notes: Perimeter is formally a Grade-3 CCSS standard; likely used here as an early-exposure/enrichment topic in this Grade-2 folder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 01 Reading Graduated Cylinders 100 mL and 500 mL
does: Three sheets (S1-S3), each with 10 graduated cylinders marked in 20 mL increments up to 100 mL; students read and write the liquid level shown on each cylinder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 02 Reading Graduated Cylinders Mixed
does: Three sheets (S1-S3), each with 10 graduated cylinders of mixed scales (whole-number increments, ranges up to 500 mL); students read and record the liquid level on each cylinder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 03 Reading Graduated Cylinders Decimals
does: Three sheets (S1-S3), each with 10 graduated cylinders marked in small increments (1-5 mL) requiring students to read decimal-valued liquid levels.
notes: Decimal-precision readings may be above typical Grade-2 level; likely an enrichment/advanced sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 04 Reading Graduated Cylinders Whole Numbers and Decimals
does: Three sheets (S1-S3), each with 10 graduated cylinders mixing whole-number and decimal-scale readings; students read and record the liquid level on each cylinder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 05 Reading Liquid Levels – 1L or 2L Jugs
does: Three sheets (S1-S3), each with 9 measuring jugs marked in 250 mL increments up to 1000 mL; students read and record the liquid level shown in each jug.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 06 Reading Liquid Levels on Measuring Jugs
does: Three sheets (S1-S3) of mixed-scale measuring jugs (some marked to 1000 mL, others to 2000 mL); students read and record the liquid level shown in each jug.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 07 Recognizing and Describing Volume Levels Full, Half-full, and Empty
does: Three-part volume worksheet: (A) students choose the word (empty/almost empty/half-full/half-empty/almost full/full) that best describes the liquid level shown in a squeeze bottle, 6 items; (B) students color containers to show a specified level (almost full, half-full, full, almost empty), 4 items; (C) students order 3 teapots by liquid level from empty to full, 3 sheets.
notes: Visually confirmed page 1 of 3, matches title Recognizing and Describing Volume Levels Full, Half-full, and Empty.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 08 Measuring Capacity Using Small Containers
does: Three sheets: Part A asks yes/no whether a shown quantity equals a target based on a given key/ratio; Part B has students determine how many small containers (cups, glasses) can be filled from a given liquid level and color them in.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 09 Comparing Capacity
does: Three sheets (Sheet 1-3), each with 5 problems comparing a capacity on the left to a total capacity on the right (expressed in customary units like pt, qt, gal, c, fl.oz, tsp, tbsp) using >, <, or =.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 10 Determining the Capacity of Each Small Container
does: Three sheets (Sheet 1-3), each with 5 problems where students determine the capacity of one small container given the combined capacity of several identical containers shown together (customary units: fl.oz, qt, c, gal, pt).

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 11 Calculating Liquid Changes in Measuring Jugs
does: Three sheets (Sheet 1-3), each with 3 problems asking students to calculate a new reading on a measuring jug (in mL) after water is added or poured out, or how much is needed to reach a target level.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 12 Estimating Capacity of Real-Life Objects
does: Three sheets: Part A has students choose the appropriate customary capacity unit (cup, pint, quart, gallon) for real-life containers; Part B sorts containers by appropriate unit; Part C fills in the blank with the correct unit in a sentence.

title: Grade 2 Math - Capacity - 13 Estimating Capacity More or Less
does: Three sheets (Sheet 1-3), each with 8 real-life objects/liquids where students choose whether the object's capacity is more or less than a given customary benchmark amount (e.g. 'less/more than 3 pints').

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 01 Writing 1 to 10 in Decreasing Order
does: Three sheets, each a themed maze/path (leading a cow, Santa, or squirrel) where students count backward by ones from 10 to 1, filling in missing numbers along the path in decreasing order.
notes: Uses US holiday character (Santa) in one sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 02 Writing 1 to 10 in Increasing Order
does: 'Ascending Order | 1 to 10' worksheet: a 5x2 grid of 10 boxes with a few numbers pre-filled at scattered positions (e.g. 1, 3, 9); students fill in the remaining boxes so the numbers 1 through 10 appear in increasing order when read across the grid.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Page is rotated 90 degrees in the PDF (landscape grid); no colouring/theme elements, plain grid worksheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 03 Write the numbers in Order 10 More 10 Less
does: Three sheets (Sheet 1-3), each with 5 problems where students fill in a sequence of numbers using 'ten more' and 'ten less' steps from a given starting number.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 04 Compare Using Symbols
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers': 14 pairs of 3-digit numbers per sheet; students write >, <, or = in the blank oval between each pair.
notes: Confirms 3-digit numbers. 3 sheets, 14 comparison pairs per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 05 Circling the Greater Smaller Number
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' worksheet with 3 sections per sheet: (A) write >, <, or = for 8 number pairs, (B) circle the greater number in each of 4 pairs, (C) circle the smaller number in each of 4 pairs; all numbers are 3-digit.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Combines symbol-writing and circling in one sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 06 Comparison Words and Symbols
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' worksheet, part A: 10 pairs of 3-digit numbers compared with >, <, or = in a blank oval; part B: 5 pairs of 3-digit numbers where students write out the comparison phrase ('is greater than', 'is less than', or 'is equal to') on a blank line.
notes: Confirms title and 3-digit numbers. 3 sheets.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 07 Cut-and-Glue Activities
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' cut-and-glue activity: 8 pairs of 3-digit numbers per sheet with a themed picture (e.g. an alligator/'Snappy' whose open mouth points to the greater number); students cut out and glue the alligator-head/mouth piece at the bottom so it faces (opens toward) the greater number in each pair.
notes: Confirms cut-and-glue with 3-digit numbers; the specific 'alligator eats the greater number' theme is now identified. 3 sheets, 8 pairs per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 08 Comparison Using Real-Life Objects
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' with clip-art containers (baskets, chests, boxes) each showing a 3-digit number label; 4 pairs per sheet; students write >, <, or = on the blank line between each pair.
notes: Confirms 3-digit numbers with real-life object pictures. 3 sheets, 4 pairs per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 09 Arranging Numbers up to 100
does: Three sheets (S1-S3): Part A has students write 5 given two-digit numbers in order from least to greatest; Part B has them order 5 different two-digit numbers from greatest to least.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 10 Compare Using Base-10 Blocks
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers - Base Ten Blocks': 5 pairs per sheet, each pair showing two groups of base-ten blocks (hundreds flats, tens rods, ones cubes); students count the blocks in each group, write the value on the blank line, and write >, <, or = in the circle between them.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Uses hundreds/tens/ones blocks (3-digit values), not just tens/ones.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 11 Finding Missing Digits
does: 'Missing Digits' worksheet, part A: 6 true/false comparison statements (>, <, =) between two 3-digit numbers with one digit blank, and 2 given digit choices; students pick the correct digit to make the statement true. Part B: 2 problems with two blanks each and two given digits to place correctly.
notes: Corrects description: it is multiple-choice digit selection (given 2 options), not a free-form fill-in plus separate ordering task. 3 sheets, 6+2 problems per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 12 Spinner-Board Activity
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' spinner activity: two 8-section spinner wheels (Wheel A and Wheel B), each section showing a 3-digit number; students make a paperclip-and-pencil spinner, spin both wheels 8 times, record the two numbers, and compare them with >, <, or = in the blank box between two answer lines.
notes: Confirms 1 page/sheet (single spinner-board page). 8 comparison rounds.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 13 Cut and Glue Activity Increasing Order
does: 'Cut & Paste Activity' (Superboy theme): 5 two-digit numbers given at the bottom in cut-out boxes; students cut them out and glue them onto 5 superhero graphics arranged in a row, in increasing (least to greatest) order.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Page is landscape/rotated in the PDF; theme is a superhero boy ('Superboy') character, numbers are 2-digit.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 14 Cut and Glue Activity Decreasing Order
does: Same 'Cut & Paste Activity' (Superboy theme) as sheet 13, but numbers are glued onto the 5 graphics in decreasing (greatest to least) order.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 15 Mixed Review
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' mixed review: part A, fill in 2 given numbers plus one shown number into blanks to make a 3-number ascending/descending chain true (4 problems); part B, circle all numbers in a list of 6 that are greater/less than a given number (2 problems); part C, from a list of 6 numbers write out those less than X and those greater than Y.
notes: Confirms 'Mixed Review' with 3-digit numbers (not the 2-digit numbers seen in some other sheets in this set). 3 sheets.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 16 Ordering Numbers 2-digit
does: 'Ordering Numbers 2-digit': part A, 6 sets of five 2-digit numbers each; students write each set from least to greatest. Part B, 6 more sets of five 2-digit numbers; students write each set from greatest to least.
notes: Confirms title and format (not a grid/selection task as guessed - it's writing sets of 5 numbers in order). 3 sheets, 12 sets total per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 17 Ordering 2-digit Numbers Symbols and Data Graphs
does: Three sheets (S1-S3): Part A has students compare and order sets of 5 two-digit numbers using < or > symbols; Part B uses a bar graph (birds, favorite subjects, or stamp collections) where students rank categories from least to greatest/greatest to least and answer a question about rank.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 18 Comparing Money Amounts up to 1000
does: Three sheets, each showing 6-7 children's piggy banks with dollar amounts; students find totals and answer questions comparing amounts (who has more/less/same, ordering all amounts least to greatest or greatest to least).

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 19 Ordering Quantities
does: Three sheets, each with 4 picture sets of 3 groups of objects; students write 1-3 to rank the groups from fewest to most items, and separately from most to fewest.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 20 Comparing and Ordering Heights
does: Three sheets with real-life height scenarios (trees in feet, people/buildings in inches or feet); students order the items from shortest to tallest or vice versa and answer multi-step questions (e.g. where a new item of given height would fit, re-ordering after a substitution).
notes: Some questions require multi-step reasoning (e.g. inserting a new value into an ordered list).

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 21 Counting and Ordering U.S. Coins
does: Three sheets, each with 2 piggy-bank picture puzzles; students count US coins in each piggy bank, write the total in cents, then order the piggy banks by amount (smallest to largest) to reveal letters spelling a 'mystery animal.'

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 22 Building and Ordering Numbers
does: 'Framing & Ordering Numbers': 8 problems per sheet; each gives 3-4 digits (some repeated, e.g. '4, 2, 2 and 3') and asks students to write all the numbers that can be formed from those digits in increasing or decreasing order (alternating between problems).
notes: Corrects description: this is not building 3-digit numbers from hundreds/tens/ones counts, but forming all possible numbers from a given set of digits and ordering them. 3 sheets, 8 problems per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 23 Comparing 3-Digit Numbers Number Lines
does: 'Number Line' worksheet: 4 number lines per sheet, each showing 7 consecutive 3-digit values with some labels hidden; for each number line, students answer 4 sub-questions - two yes/no questions about relative position (left/right of a value) and two comparison questions (fill in > or < between two numbers).
notes: Confirms number-line format; clarifies the exact question types (yes/no position questions plus symbol comparisons). 3 sheets, 4 number lines x 4 questions per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 24 Cut and Glue Activity Ordering 2-digit Numbers - Increasing
does: Same 'Cut & Paste Activity' (Superboy theme, 5 graphics in a row) as sheets 13/14, with 5 two-digit numbers to cut out and glue on in increasing (least to greatest) order.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Appears to duplicate sheet 13's format/theme with a different number set.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 25 Comparing Prices Store Theme
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers' store-themed worksheet: two storefronts (Store 1, Store 2) each display 3 items with 3-digit dollar price tags (e.g. laptop $940, phone $700); 5 questions below ask students to compare prices across the two stores (which store is cheaper, how much they'd pay/save, which they'd prefer).
notes: Confirms US dollar ($) prices. 3 sheets, 6 items (3 per store) and 5 questions per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 26 Cut and Glue Activity Ordering Numbers to 20 - Decreasing O
does: 'Cut & Paste Activity' (Spiderboy theme): 5 numbers up to 20 given at the bottom (e.g. 17, 20, 5, 10, 9) in cut-out boxes; students cut them out and glue them onto 5 superhero graphics in decreasing (greatest to least) order.
notes: Corrects sheets count from 0 (no extractable text) to 3, confirmed visually. Same format as the Superboy cut-and-glue sheets (13/14/24) but Spiderboy-themed and numbers up to 20 instead of 2-digit numbers generally.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 27 Word Problems MCQs
does: Three sheets, each with 6 multiple-choice word problems (choice a or b) involving comparing two 3-digit quantities in real-life scenarios (contest scores, paint cans, school populations, shipments); some problems include a 'later it was found a digit was wrong' twist requiring re-comparison.
notes: A few problems embed a digit-correction twist, adding light critical-thinking difficulty.

title: Grade 2 Math - Comparing & Ordering Numbers - 28 Comparing 3-Digit Numbers MCQs
does: 'Comparing 3-Digit Numbers - MCQ': 7 multiple-choice questions per sheet with 3-4 answer options each, mixing question types - identify which number is greater/equal/not-greater-than a given value, choose the correct comparison symbol or word, or pick a number that completes an inequality.
notes: Confirms MCQ format and title; question variety is broader than simple 'larger/smaller' selection. 3 sheets, 7 questions per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Counting - 01 Classify, Count, and Compare
does: 'Count and Compare': a large oval scene mixing 4 animal types (e.g. rhinos, lions, elephants, giraffes) in random arrangement; students count how many of each animal, answer which type has the most/fewest, and answer 'how many more/fewer' comparison questions between two specific animal types.
notes: Confirms title and format. 3 sheets, 4 animal categories per sheet, 4 count blanks + most/fewest + 2 more/fewer questions.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 01 Reading Bar Graphs Three Categories
does: Each sheet shows two already-drawn bar graphs with three categories (e.g. flowers, vehicles). Students read the height of each bar by counting squares and write the count for each category into a matching table.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Flowers and Vehicles); simpler than a word-problem format — no comparison/how-many-more questions, just reading each bar's value into a table.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 02 Reading Bar Graphs Four Categories
does: Students read an already-completed bar graph with four categories (e.g. Toy Shop sales: car, elephant, duck, drum) and answer 5 questions per sheet: read a named bar's value, find the difference between two bars, identify the tallest bar, sum two bars, and compare two bars directly.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Andy's Toy Shop).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 03 Reading Bar Graphs Several Categories
does: Students read an already-completed bar graph with five categories and a scale in intervals of 5 (e.g. Favorite Subjects: Social Studies, Math, Science, ELA, Others) and answer 5 questions per sheet: identify the scale/unit used, find the second most popular, compare two bars, identify which bar has a given value, and find bars with equal values.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Favorite Subjects); scale counts by 5s up to 60.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 04 Reading Picture Graph
does: Students read a picture graph (grid of stacked animal/object icons, one icon = one item, e.g. Richard's Farm Animals) and answer questions: which category has fewest, count a named category, compare two categories, identify a category with a given count, and find the total.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Richard's Farm Animals); 1 icon = 1 item, no separate key box.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 05 Reading Pictograph Moderate Level
does: Students read an already-completed pictograph (e.g. Pumpkin Harvest) where each symbol = a multiple such as 50 and a half symbol represents half that value, then answer 5 questions per sheet: who has most, read a named value, identify who has a given value, find equal values, and verify a true/false comparison statement.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Pumpkin Harvest); key = 50 pumpkins per icon, with half-icons shown for values that are not exact multiples.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 06 Making Bar Graphs
does: Given a small data table with 3 categories (e.g. Eddie's baking: pies 4, cookies 3, cupcakes 9), students color the correct number of boxes on a pre-scaled grid (0-10) to build a bar graph matching the data.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (baking for the fair).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 07 Counting and Creating Bar Graphs
does: A picture scene shows scattered insects of 3 kinds (e.g. ladybug, ant, caterpillar). Students count the insects of each kind, then create a bar graph by coloring the correct number of squares on a pre-scaled grid (0-10).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (insects scene).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 08 Counting and Drawing Bar Graphs
does: A picture scene shows scattered accessory items of a few kinds (e.g. hats, gift boxes, sunglasses, handbags). Students count the items of each kind, then draw bars on a pre-scaled grid (0-10) to complete a bar graph.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (accessories scene).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 09 Drawing and Interpreting Bar Graphs Four Categories
does: Given a data table with four categories (e.g. Garden Creatures: ladybug 7, grasshopper 3, dragonfly 5, butterfly 9), students draw bars on a pre-scaled grid (0-10) to represent the data, then answer 4 questions per sheet (read a value, compare two categories, identify greatest, identify fewest).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Garden Creatures).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 10 Tally Marks and Bar Graphs
does: Given a tally chart of 5 categories (e.g. school supplies: book, pencil, eraser, backpack, stapler), students count the tally marks for each item and draw bars on a pre-scaled grid (0-10) to build a bar graph matching the tally counts.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (school supplies).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 11 Title, Labeling Axis, Scaling and Graphing
does: Given a data table with 5 categories (e.g. Little Pets survey: snails 8, lizards 14, rats 12, chameleons 4, frogs 18), students build a complete bar graph on a fully blank grid: write a title, label both axes, choose an appropriate scale, and draw the bars.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Little Pets); grid, title box and axis-label blanks are all empty, unlike other sheets in this folder that provide a pre-scaled grid.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 12 Drawing and Interpreting Bar Graphs
does: Given a data table with 5 categories and larger values (e.g. Musical Instrument sales: 630, 720, 405, 540, 405), students draw bars on a pre-scaled grid (0-900, gridlines every 90) to represent the data, then answer 4 word-problem questions per sheet (difference, equal values, difference between two, total).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Musical Instruments); grid is pre-scaled with large intervals of 90.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 13 Relative Frequency and Percent Bar Graphs
does: Two-part percent bar graph worksheet: (A) given a frequency table (counts out of 40 total), students compute relative frequency as a percent and draw bars on a percent (0-50%) bar graph; (B) students read a completed percent bar graph of survey data and answer 3 word-problem questions (counts, comparisons, totals), 3 sheets.
notes: Visually confirmed page 1 of 3, matches title Relative Frequency and Percent Bar Graphs. Content level (percent calculations) is notably more advanced than a typical Grade 2 topic despite the folder label.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 14 Counting - Tally Graphs
does: Students read a tally chart (e.g. Weekend Sale of burger, pizza, fried chicken, hot dog) and answer 5 questions per sheet: read a named category's count from the tally marks, identify most sold, find the difference between two categories, identify least sold, and find the total sold.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Weekend Sale); this sheet only reads a tally chart directly, it does not involve drawing a separate graph.

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 15 Interpreting Line Graph Easy
does: Students study an already-drawn line graph plotting a value against days of the week (e.g. Car Sales Monday-Friday) and answer 5 questions per sheet: total over all days, identify the day of max value, read a named day's value, identify the day of min value, and find the difference between two days.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Car Sales).

title: Grade 2 Math - Data & Graphs - 16 Drawing Line Graph Easy
does: Given a small data table (e.g. Movies Watched by year, 2008-2012), students plot the points on a pre-drawn, pre-scaled and pre-labeled grid and connect them to draw a line graph.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Movies Watched); grid axes are already scaled/labeled, only the plotting is left to the student.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 80 Let's Go Shopping!

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 84 Buying with Notes and Coins

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 86 What's the Change
does: Students count pictured coins offered for a priced item (all under $1, in cents) and write the change returned, 7 items per sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 87 Paying using minimum American Coins & Bills
does: Students are given a priced item (5 per sheet, $20-$280) and must draw/select the fewest possible American bills and coins to pay for it exactly.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 88 Making Change
does: For pictured items with prices (mostly under $50, a few word problems up to $89.99), students record the bill paid and compute the change due; items 1-6 are picture-based, 7-8 are text word problems.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 89 Making Change
does: For a themed store (toys, food, sporting goods), students identify the price of a pictured item a named customer buys, given the amount paid, then compute the change received; 5 items per sheet, round bills of $5-$100.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 90 Expressing Money in Words Up to $100
does: "Money in Words" - 8 dollar amounts per sheet are given as figures (e.g. $67.28); students write each amount out in words on the two blank lines below. Amounts range up to $100.
notes: 3 sheets, 8 problems each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 91 Expressing Money in Figures Up to $1000
does: "Money in Words" - 8 dollar-and-cents amounts per sheet are given written out in words (e.g. 'seventy-two dollars and ninety-eight cents'); students write each amount in dollar figures (e.g. $72.98) on the blank line below. Amounts range up to $1,000.
notes: 3 sheets, 8 problems each. Amounts up to $1000 (beyond typical Grade 2 CCSS range of $1.00).

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 92 Are the items affordable
does: Students calculate the total money pictured in a named child's bank, then check off which of 5 pictured items (with prices) that amount is enough to buy.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 93 Making Change - Theme
does: For a themed store (food, sporting goods, home appliances), students identify the price of a pictured item a named customer buys given the amount paid, then compute the change received; 5 items per sheet, round bills of $5-$100.
notes: Near-identical format/content to sheet 89 'Making Change', different store themes.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 94 Australian Money MCQ
does: Students look at pictured notes and coins and select the total amount from four lettered multiple-choice answers, with totals ranging roughly $8 to $351.
notes: Title says Australian Money MCQ but currency symbol shown is a generic dollar sign; totals go well beyond typical Grade 2 range (up to $351), suggesting a review/challenge sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 95 Identifying the Coins and Their Values
does: "Coins - Name" - for each of 4 pictured US coins per sheet (quarter, nickel, dime, penny), students write the coin's name and its value on the blank lines provided.
notes: 3 sheets, 4 coins each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 96 Counting Coins
does: "Counting Coins" - 3-part sheet: (1) count 5 sets of pictured US coins (pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters, half-dollars) and write the total dollar amount; (2) 4 problems adding named quantities of coin types (e.g. '5 dimes + 4 quarters'); (3) 2 word problems totaling a mixed set of coins from a story context.
notes: 3 sheets, 11 problems each (5 count, 4 add-quantities, 2 word problems). Includes half-dollar coins, which are less commonly covered.

title: Grade 2 Math - Money - 97 American Currency Chart - up to $1
does: "U.S. Money" reference chart - a single table showing the obverse and reverse images of the penny, nickel, dime, quarter, half-dollar, and $1 bill, with each one's value labeled (1 cent, 5 cents, 10 cents, 25 cents, 50 cents, $1). Not a problem set.
notes: 1 page only, a reference/poster chart with no problems to solve, consistent with there being no answer key.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 01 Identifying Sentences & Drawing Groups Level 1
does: Two-part sheet. Part A: 4 multiple-choice items showing equal-groups picture models (e.g. 4 boxes of 2 stars); students pick the matching multiplication sentence from 4 options (a-d). Part B: 2 items give a multiplication sentence (e.g. 2x4=___) and students draw the equal groups (empty shapes) to find and illustrate the answer.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Identify-L1S1); title on sheet is Equal Groups: Multiplication Sentence.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 02 Identifying Sentences & Drawing Groups Level 2
does: Two-part sheet, Level 2 (larger factors up to 10). Part A: 4 multiple-choice items showing equal-groups picture models (e.g. 3 ovals of 6 dots, 4 pentagons of 7 triangles, 2 rows of 10 hearts); students pick the matching multiplication sentence from 4 options (a-d). Part B: 2 items give a multiplication sentence (e.g. 7x3=___, 4x9=___) and students draw the equal groups to find the answer.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Identify-L2S1); harder numbers than sibling Level 1 sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 03 Multiplication for Beginners Factors up to 10
does: Basic vertical multiplication facts with factors up to 10, plus 1-2 word problems per sheet (e.g. eggs per tray x number of trays, pencils per case x number of cases).
notes: 3 sheets, 12-14 vertical problems plus 1-2 word problems each; intro-level.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 04 Multiplying by 2, 5, or 10
does: Section A: find the product for facts limited to the 2, 5, or 10 times tables, plus one word problem filling in a number-of-groups/size/total template. Section B: multiple-choice word problems (e.g. total price at $10 each, tulips per bouquet).
notes: 3 sheets; each has 4 fact problems, 1 fill-in word problem, and 3 MCQ word problems.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 05 Multiplying by 2, 3, 4, or 5
does: Section A: find the product for facts limited to 2,3,4,5 times tables. Section B: word problems filling in a table (boxes/packs x items-per-box = total). Section C: compare two multiplication expressions and check yes/no to a greater/lesser question.
notes: 3 sheets, each with 4 fact problems, 2 table word problems, 1-2 yes/no comparison problems.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 06 Multiplying Numbers from 1 to 12
does: Vertical multiplication fact drill with both factors up to 12 (e.g. 12x6, 11x9), purely numeric.
notes: 5 sheets, 15 problems each. Factors up to 12 exceed typical Grade 2 CCSS scope.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 07 Describing Equal Groups
does: Each sheet has 2 equal-groups picture models (e.g. 4 trees with 4 fruits each; 2 cages with 2 rabbits each). For each model students answer 4 guided questions: number of groups, number of items per group, write the multiplication sentence describing the model, and the total number of items.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1), titled Describing Model: Equal Groups.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 08 Multiplication Using Pictures
does: Word problems with a picture of one item repeated (e.g. a tray of eggs, a flower) asking how many total parts (e.g. petals, eggs) across a given number of copies; students multiply items-per-picture by number of pictures.
notes: 3 sheets, 8 problems each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 09 Finding the Total Cost
does: Word problems: given a unit price (e.g. $9 per item, shown on a price tag picture) and a quantity (e.g. 8 items), students multiply to find the total cost.
notes: 3 sheets, ~8 problems each; each item shown as a picture with a price tag.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 10 Finding Missing Factors
does: Themed 'hen and eggs' matching activity: given a product on the hen, students pick the two egg factors from a set that multiply to give it (e.g. hen shows 12, eggs are 4,6,7,9... student finds e.g. 4x3 or matching pair).
notes: 3 sheets, 5 problems each; products range higher in later sheets (up to 182 on sheet 3), suggesting factors beyond single digits for some items.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 11 Drawing Multiplication Arrays
does: Sheet shows a worked example (4x10 array of dots = 40) followed by 6 multiplication sentences (e.g. 3x5=___, 8x4=___, up to 3x11=___). Students draw a rectangular array of dots/objects in the blank space to find each product.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1), titled Drawing Arrays. Total pages is 3.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 12 Writing Multiplication Sentences with Equal Groups Easy
does: Each sheet shows 5 equal-groups picture models (e.g. 2 vases of flowers, 4 bunches of balloons, 3 birdcages, 2 stacks of books, 3 clumps of mushrooms). Students write a full multiplication sentence (groups x items per group = total) describing each model. Easy tier: small group counts and small items-per-group.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Write-L1S1), titled Equal Groups: Multiplication Sentence; Easy difficulty tier.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 13 Repeated Addition to Multiplication
does: Given a repeated addition sentence (e.g. 3+3+3), students write it as a multiplication sentence and find the product, factors up to 9.
notes: 3 sheets, 15 problems each, purely numeric.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 14 Multiplication and Comparison Cut-and-Glue Activity
does: Alligator-jaw themed cut-and-glue: for each multiplication expression (e.g. 3x8) paired with a number (e.g. 30), students decide which quantity is greater and glue the correct 'jaw' picture in the matching box; factors up to 10.
notes: 3 sheets, 16 problems each, themed cut-and-glue (needs scissors/glue, not just pencil).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 15 Multiplication and Comparison Using Symbols
does: Students write <, >, or = to compare a multiplication expression (e.g. 10x4) to a given number (e.g. 36), factors up to 10.
notes: 3 sheets, 14 problems each, purely numeric.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 16 Multiplication within 100 Standard
does: Vertical (standard algorithm layout) single-digit x single/double-digit multiplication facts with products within 100, factors up to 10.
notes: 5 sheets, 15 problems each, purely numeric drill.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 17 Writing Multiplication Sentences Level 1
does: Each sheet shows 8 rectangular arrays of pictures (rows x columns, e.g. 4x2 sundaes, 3x2 pitchers, 3x4 whistles, 2x3 pears, 3x3 phones, 4x2 spoons, 2x4 cups, 4x3 watches). Students write a multiplication sentence (rows x columns = total) describing each array. Level 1 uses small factors (max ~4x4).
notes: Confirmed by viewing pages 1-2 (L1S1, L1S2); labeled 'Multiplication Sentence: Arrays' worksheet from mathworksheets4kids.com.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 18 Writing Multiplication Sentences Level 2
does: Each sheet shows 7 rectangular arrays of pictures with larger dimensions than the Level 1 sibling sheet (e.g. 3x9 hearts, 8x9 squares, 6x6 hexagons, up to about 10x8). Students write a multiplication sentence (rows x columns = total) describing each array.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (L2S1), titled Multiplication Sentence: Arrays; larger factors than the Level 1 sheet (17).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 19 Completing Multiplication Sentences Level 1
does: Each sheet shows 8 rectangular arrays of pictures (rows x columns, e.g. 4x2 strawberries, 3x3 broccoli, 3x5 lollipops). The multiplication equation is given with the product and one blank factor (either rows or columns); students find the missing factor, e.g. 4 x ___ = 8. Level 1 uses small arrays.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (L1S1), titled Completing Multiplication Equations; uses arrays of objects, not equal-groups clusters.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 20 Completing Multiplication Sentences Level 2
does: Each sheet shows 7 rectangular arrays of pictures with larger dimensions (e.g. 7x4 squares, 10x6 stars, 8x8 symbols, up to 12x6 clovers). The multiplication equation is given with the product and one blank factor; students find the missing factor, e.g. ___x4=28. Level 2 uses bigger arrays than the Level 1 sibling sheet.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (L2S1), titled Completing Multiplication Equations; larger factors than sheet 19 (Level 1).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 21 Rectangular Array of Squares Writing & Drawing
does: Mixed area-model sheet, 2 parts. Part A: 4 grids with a shaded rectangle (e.g. 4x3, 3x9); students write the multiplication sentence describing it. Part B: 4 multiplication sentences (e.g. 7x6=___, 11x5=___) with a blank grid; students draw/shade the area model to find the product.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Mixed:S1), titled Multiplication Sentence - Area. Total pages is 3, not the 5 the catalogue guessed.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 22 Writing Multiplication Sentences with Equal Groups Moderate
does: Students write a full multiplication sentence (axb=c) describing each equal-groups picture model shown; moderate difficulty level.
notes: 3 sheets (S1-S3), 5 problems each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 23 Completing Multiplication Sentences with Equal Groups Level 1
does: Each sheet shows 5 equal-groups picture models (e.g. 2 bowls of 3 oranges, 4 boxes of crayons, 3 plates of 4 strawberries). The multiplication equation is given with one blank (either the number of groups or the number per group) and the product filled in; students find the missing factor, e.g. blank x 3 = 6.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Complete-L1S1); title 'Equal Groups: Multiplication Sentence'.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 24 Completing Multiplication Sentences with Equal Groups Level 2
does: Students look at a picture model of equal groups and complete a multiplication equation with a missing factor (e.g. 6x?=30), products up to 45 (single-digit factors up to 9).
notes: 3 sheets (S1-S3), 5 problems each, similar difficulty across sheets.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 25 Writing Multiplication Sentences Rectangular Array of Squares
does: Each sheet shows 9 grids with a shaded rectangular region (varying rows x columns, e.g. 6x4, 3x2, 4x10). Students count the rows and columns of the shaded rectangle and write a multiplication sentence (rows x columns = area/total squares) for each model.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Write:S1), titled Multiplication Sentence - Area; distinct from the rectangular-array-of-objects sheets (this uses a shaded grid, no pictures).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 26 Drawing Arrays on Grids and Completing the Multiplication Sentences
does: Each sheet gives 9 multiplication sentences with a blank grid beside each (e.g. 10x2=___, 7x4=___, 3x9=___, up to 5x11=___). Students draw/shade a rectangular area model on the grid with the given dimensions and use it to find the product.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Draw:S1), titled Multiplication Sentence - Area; companion sheet to the read-the-area-model version (sheet 25).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 27 Repeated Addition Sentences in Two Ways
does: Students rewrite each multiplication sentence (e.g. 8x3) as a repeated-addition sentence in two possible ways (grouping by either factor), factors up to 10.
notes: 3 sheets, 9-10 problems each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 28 Completing Multiplication Sentences
does: Students fill in a missing factor or missing product to complete a multiplication equation, factors up to 10 (e.g. _x9=27, 7x_=35).
notes: 3 sheets, 14 problems each, purely numeric (no pictures).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 29 Single-digit Multiplication Word Problems
does: Each sheet has 5 single-digit multiplication word problems in varied real-world contexts (e.g. batteries per flashlight, tracks per CD, area of a rectangle given length and width, cookies per ounce of butter with a two-step scale-up, liters of oil across a fleet of cars). Students write and solve the equation on a blank line.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1); item 3 explicitly covers rectangle area, item 4 requires a two-step scale-up (ounce->8 ounces).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 30 Single-Digit Multiplication Real-Life Problems
does: Word problems using single-digit multiplication in real-life contexts (flower vases, saplings per year, rectangle area = length x width, distance walked per hour) with factors up to 10.
notes: 3 sheets, 5 word problems each; one problem (rectangle area) is above typical Grade 2 scope (area is a Grade 3 standard).

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 31 Equivalent Multiplication Sentences MCQs
does: Multiple-choice: students choose which option(s) among a,b,c,d are equivalent to a given multiplication sentence (commutative property, e.g. 2x4 equivalent to 4x2), factors up to 10.
notes: 3 sheets, 7 MCQ items each; some answer choices may allow multiple correct selections.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 32 Multiplication With Word Problems Factors up to 12
does: Students solve vertical multiplication problems with one factor up to 12 (e.g. 8x2, 10x6), plus 2 word problems per sheet involving repeated groups (e.g. juice glasses per day over a week, check leaves per book, flash cards per case).
notes: 3 sheets, 12 vertical problems + 2 word problems each. Factors go up to 12, beyond typical Grade 2 CCSS scope (facts to 10x10 or less); more Grade 3 level.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 33 Multiplication Models - Equal Groups
does: Each sheet has 2 equal-groups picture models (e.g. 4 trees with fruit, 2 cages of rabbits, 2 nests of eggs, 3 flowerpots). For each model students answer 4 guided questions: number of groups, number of items per group, write the multiplication sentence describing the model, and the total number of items.
notes: Confirmed by viewing pages 1-2 (Sheet 1, Sheet 2), titled Describing Model: Equal Groups; same worksheet series/format as sheet 07 in this folder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 34 Repeated Addition and Multiplication
does: Each sheet gives 15 repeated-addition expressions (e.g. 3+3+3, 5+5+5+5, 9+9). Students convert each to a multiplication sentence by filling in the number of addends (the missing factor) and then find the product, e.g. ___x3=___ for 3+3+3.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Easy:S1), titled Repeated Addition.

title: Grade 2 Math - Multiplication - 35 Number Line Multiplication
does: Each item gives a jump size and number of jumps (e.g. '4' and '3'); students draw equal hops on a 0-20 number line to reach the product and write the multiplication sentence, numbers within 20.
notes: 5 sheets, 6 number-line problems each, products stay within 0-20.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 01 Match Number Lines with Multiplication Sentences
does: Each sheet shows 5 number lines with hops of equal size (skip-counting arcs) and 5 multiplication sentences (e.g. 1x15=15, 5x2=10, 3x6=18, 4x8=32). Students match each number line to its equivalent multiplication sentence based on hop size and number of hops.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1), titled Number Line Vs Multiplication Sentence (landscape page).

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 02 Identifying Whole Numbers Type 2 Level 1
does: Each sheet shows 7 number lines with consecutive whole numbers counting by 1, with some numbers given and some replaced by blank boxes at varying tick positions (e.g. 2, 3, [ ], 5, [ ], [ ], 8, [ ]). Students fill in the missing whole numbers to complete the sequence. Level 1 of the Type 2 (blank-box) missing-numbers format.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T2L1S1), titled Missing Numbers; this is basic counting-by-1 number-line practice, not related to multiplication despite being filed under the Multiplication/Number Lines topic.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 03 Identifying Whole Numbers Type 2 Level 2
does: Each sheet shows 7 number lines with evenly-spaced tick marks where only a couple of numbers are given (e.g. 4...7...[ ][ ][ ][ ]; 0...[ ]...[ ]...18) and students must first work out the constant interval from the given values/spacing, then fill in all missing numbers. Level 2 is harder than the Level 1 sibling sheet (fewer given numbers, larger/non-obvious intervals).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T2L2S1), titled Missing Numbers; general number-line skill, not multiplication-specific.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 04 Draw Hops on the Number Line Type 1
does: Each item gives a jump size and number of jumps (e.g. hop of 4, 3 times); students draw equal hops on a 0-20 number line to find the product and complete a multiplication sentence.
notes: 5 sheets, 6 problems each; number lines run 0-20 on every sheet.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 05 Draw Hops on the Number Line Type 2
does: Each sheet gives a worked example (7x3=21 shown as hops on a number line) followed by 5 multiplication sentences (e.g. 5x2=___, 8x6=___, 4x9=___) with a blank number line pre-labeled with tick marks scaled to the hop size. Students draw/indicate the hops on the number line and complete the multiplication sentence. Type 2 uses larger factors/scales than the Type 1 sibling sheet.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T2S1), titled Number Line Multiplication.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 06 Draw Number Lines
does: Each sheet gives 6 text instructions for drawing a number line from scratch, specifying a start value, end value, and either a number of equal intervals or a fixed increment (e.g. Draw a number line from 0 to 10 with ten equal intervals; Draw a number line from 3 to 13 with increments of 2). Students draw the blank number line with correctly spaced tick marks and labels in the space provided.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1), titled Number Line. General number-line construction skill, not specific to multiplication despite sitting in the Number Lines/Multiplication folder.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 07 Number Line Fill in the Missing Numbers Type 1
does: Each sheet shows 6 number lines (0-20 scale) with equal-size hops. A multiplication sentence beneath each has one blank, which could be either factor OR the product (e.g. 2x___=6, ___x4=16, 9x2=___); students use the number line model to find the missing value. Type 1 uses a smaller 0-20 number line than the Type 2 sibling sheet.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T1S1), titled Multiplication Sentence - Missing Numbers; any of factor/factor/product can be the blank, not just the factor as sheet 08 (Type 2) shows.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 08 Number Line Fill in the Missing Numbers Type 2
does: Each sheet shows 6 number lines with equal-size skip-count hops (e.g. hops of 5 to 20, hops of 7 to 63, hops of 9 to 81). Below each number line a multiplication sentence is given with one blank factor and the product filled in (e.g. ___x5=20, 9x___=63); students find the missing factor by counting the hops or the hop size.
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T2S1); actual worksheet title is Multiplication Sentence - Missing Numbers, not a fill-in-the-missing-numbers-on-the-number-line sheet as the filename suggested.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 09 Multiplication using Number Line - MCQs
does: Each sheet shows 6 number lines with equal-size skip-count hops. Students identify the correct multiplication sentence for each from 4 multiple-choice options (a-d), which include distractor sentences with swapped/incorrect factors (e.g. 6x5=30 vs 8x5=40).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (Sheet 1), titled Number Line Multiplication - MCQ.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 10 Write the Multiplication Sentences Type 1
does: Each sheet shows 6 number lines on a 0-20 scale with equal-size skip-count hops. Students write the full multiplication sentence (number of hops x hop size = endpoint) describing each number line, all three blanks to fill in. Type 1 uses a smaller 0-20 scale than the Type 2 sibling sheet (11).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T1S1), titled Multiplication Sentence.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Lines - 11 Write the Multiplication Sentences Type 2
does: Each sheet shows 6 number lines (larger scales, e.g. 0-36, 0-84, 0-108) with equal-size skip-count hops. Students write the full multiplication sentence (number of hops x hop size = endpoint) describing each number line, with all three blanks to fill in. Type 2 uses larger scales/hop sizes than the Type 1 sibling sheet (10).
notes: Confirmed by viewing page 1 (T2S1), titled Multiplication Sentence.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 01 Odd and Even
does: Two-digit numbers are listed in two groups of 18. Part A: students circle all the odd numbers in the first group. Part B: students circle all the even numbers in the second group.
notes: Confirmed by viewing the single page, titled Identify: Odd & Even. Total pages is 1, not the 2 the catalogue had.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 02 Group in Pairs
does: Students circle pictured objects in groups of two (pairs) and then write whether the total count is odd or even.
notes: 3 sheets, 5 problems each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 03 Writing Odd or Even
does: Students look at a 2-3 digit number and write whether it is odd or even.
notes: 3 sheets, 16 problems each, purely numeric, 2-3 digit numbers.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 04 Grouping the Items
does: Students draw/circle groups of pictured items (flowers, onions, papayas, etc.) to form two groups matching a stated odd/even requirement (e.g. 'create two groups of an odd number of onions').
notes: 3 sheets, 6 instructions each.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 05 Sum and Difference
does: Multiple choice: students reason about whether a sum/difference of odd/even numbers is odd or even without calculating (e.g. odd+odd=even), then apply that rule to classify sums/differences of specific 2-3 digit numbers (up to 3 digits, e.g. 943+716) as odd or even without computing.
notes: 3 sheets, 4 MCQ rule questions + 8 apply-the-rule problems each; numbers go up to 3 digits, more abstract/advanced than typical single-digit odd/even work.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 06 Is the Product Odd or Even
does: Multiple choice: students reason about whether a product of odd/even factors is odd or even without multiplying, then apply the rule to classify specific single-digit multiplication products (factors up to 10, e.g. 5x8) as odd or even without computing.
notes: 3 sheets, 4 MCQ rule questions + 8 apply-the-rule problems each; requires understanding multiplication, more advanced than basic odd/even identification.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 07 Forming Odd Even Numbers
does: Part A: from 3-4 given digits, students form the largest/smallest odd or even number possible. Part B: students list all possible odd or even numbers that can be formed from 3 given digits.
notes: 3 sheets, 4 Part A + 4 Part B problems each; more advanced/abstract than typical Grade 2 odd/even identification tasks.

title: Grade 2 Math - Number Sense - 08 Writing Double Facts
does: Students complete a doubles addition fact for a given even number (e.g. 8 = __ + __), plus 2 word problems per sheet applying doubles/halving to real scenarios (splitting marbles evenly, sharing a movie ticket cost).
notes: 3 sheets, 8 fact problems + 2 word problems each.
